scope: Proposition 2.3 of the manuscript “The Penrose inequality for maximal asymptotically hyperbolic initial data” (preprints/The-Penrose-inequality-for-maximal-asymptotically-hyperbolic-initial-data-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 641d4aa3892adbca), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose g−b ∈ C2,α τ , τ > 3/2, and ∫︁ V0|Rg +6| dVg < ∞ on the end. The fluxes (1.3) transform as a Lorentz covector under hyperbolic isometries of the asymptotic chart. Such chart changes preserve the weighted decay and integrability hypotheses used here. Consequently a future-timelike original covector admits a chart with p0 = mAH and p1 = p2 = p3 = 0.
